study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used quantile linear regression to estimate the normative range by calculating 5th, 50th (median), and 95th percentile regression curves with bootstrapping confidence intervals. Sex-specific normative age models were constructed under 10-fold cross-validation.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used quantile linear regression to estimate the normative range (Allen et al. 2014; Jing et al. 2023; Lin et al. 2023). To quantify the normative model, we estimated the 50th (median) percentile regression curves with bootstrapping confidence intervals. To avoid bias in the model, we computed the normative range by estimating the 5th and 95th percentiles in regression models.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Lin2024.pdf.md: Normative modeling for dynamic FC features section

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Two types of functional connectivity features were modeled: (1) aFCS - average FC connection strength (mean of FC strength from all window-wise FC matrices, representing static FC), and (2) fFCS - fluctuation characteristic of connection strength (average change of the window-wise FC strength, representing dynamic FC variability). FC matrices were computed between all pairs of regions of the Human Brainnetome Atlas and decomposed into 17 networks based on Yeo-17 network template. Each individual's dynamic FC pattern was represented by 34 features (17 networks x 2 measures).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The average FC connection strength (aFCS, mean of FC strength from all window-wise FC matrices) and fluctuation characteristic of connection strength (fFCS, average change of the window-wise FC strength) for each Yeo-17 network was yielded from time-varying dynamic FC matrices. Finally, each individual's dynamic FC pattern was represented by 34 features.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Lin2024.pdf.md: Calculate dynamic FC pattern section

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Sex-specific normative age models were built. Age was used as the predictor variable in quantile regression, and separate models were estimated for female and male groups to avoid potential sex effects on model construction.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Based on the large public data set Cam-CAN, we estimated sex-specific normative age models for each dynamic FC feature... To avoid the potential sex effects on model construction, we separately estimated the normative model in female/male groups.
